config_text:
# The serving config for the editor flow (0008): config/tuned.env, plus the half of
# the winning config that is per-request everywhere else.
#
# The scorer sends sampling and the thinking toggle on every request. Claude Code
# sends its own body and neither of them, so through /v1/messages the only place the
# settled config can live is the server's defaults. Served without these, this model
# thinks at `xhigh` by default — which 0005 measured as no better and four times the
# wall clock, and which three tier-1 tasks never terminated at.
#
# The context is 49,152 rather than the scorer's 32,768, and that is capacity rather than
# tuning: an editor session's first request measured 36,309 tokens — the tool set, the
# project's own instructions and the editor's context — which does not fit 32,768 before
# anybody types. 0014's attended ceiling is 57,344 and 65,536 made the desktop unusable;
# 49,152 sits under both and leaves ~13k for the work.
#
# Raising it buys nothing in speed. Prefill costs what the prompt is, not what the context
# reserves: that 36,309-token turn took 434 s of ingest at either size.
MODEL_HF="bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M"
HOST="127.0.0.1"
PORT="8081"
CTX_SIZE="49152"
CACHE_TYPE_K="q8_0"
CACHE_TYPE_V="q8_0"
FLASH_ATTN="auto"
N_GPU_LAYERS="999"
PARALLEL="1"
JINJA="1"

# The prefill batch is deliberately unset here too, and on this profile there is nothing to
# buy: cold ingest at depth spanned 0.5% across everything it admits — 573 s at 512 against
# 570 at 1024 and 2048 — on the profile whose 434 s of ingest motivated measuring it at all.
# 4096 is inadmissible: the allocator fails on the first prefill batch.

# 0005's settled pair for thinking off. `enable_thinking` is the model's own template
# kwarg — the same mechanism config/profiles/qwen3.8.json names, so this serves what
# the scorer measured rather than something adjacent to it.
CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS='{"enable_thinking":false}'
TEMP="0.7"
TOP_P="0.80"
TOP_K="20"
PRESENCE_PENALTY="1.5"

# Claude Code sends a `role: "system"` message after the user turn — the
# `mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07` capability, sent on every request whether 21
# tools are defined or none. The model's own template raises on it, which llama.cpp
# returns as a 500 and Claude Code retries ten times and gives up. The override differs
# from the shipped template in one line: a non-leading system message renders as its own
# ChatML system block instead of raising.
CHAT_TEMPLATE_FILE="config/templates/qwen3.8-system-anywhere.jinja"

# The endpoint's own counters, off by default in llama.cpp. Every config here that a
# measurement was taken on sets it, and this is the one actually run day to day: without it
# the decode rate behind a slow session has to be reconstructed from transcript timestamps,
# which is how it was measured the first time this config was profiled.
METRICS="1"
llama_server:
version: 0.3.0 (build 10621, commit c1d0e7a00)
built with AppleClang 17.0.0.17000604 for Darwin arm64
sampling: configured temperature 0.7, top_p 0.80, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5; thinking disabled; no per-run overrides
sessions: fresh chains, one session each, 24 tool-call cap, 20-minute per-session bound
runtime_limits: First baseline overlapped with make check for part of its reading phase. Machine load and prompt-cache reuse are not controlled; elapsed times are descriptive, not a speed benchmark.
observed_session_budget: Localcode reported a 27648-token handoff ceiling in the first baseline; its final account reported 30168 of 45056 tokens. Server context is 49152. Preserve logs rather than treating these distinct limits as one number.
